chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Yaqoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about breast-feeding, what is the least amount that makes marriage prohibited? He said: 'That which builds the flesh or the blood.' Then he said: 'Do you consider one (feeding) to build it?' I said: 'I ask you, may Allah improve you, (what about) two?' He said: 'No.' So I did not cease to count for him until it reached ten feedings.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of breast-feeding required to prohibit marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential debate regarding the minimum quantity of milk required to establish the mahram relationship through radhāʿ, highlighting the Imam's nuanced approach to defining 'nourishment.' While acknowledging that a single feeding can theoretically suffice if it nourishes, the dialogue with Ubayd ibn Zurarah demonstrates the practical application of the 'ten feedings' (or ten distinct suckles) standard often cited in Shia fiqh to ensure certainty. This narration underscores the importance of distinguishing between the theoretical minimum and the sufficient quantity for legal certainty in family law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Yaqoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the breast-feeding, what is the least of what it Prohibits from (marriage). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What builds the flesh, or the blood’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you see one (breast-feeding) would build it?’ So I said, ‘I ask you<sup>asws</sup>, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well, (what about) two (sessions of breast-feeding)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. So I did not cease to reiterate upon it until it reached ten breast feeding sessions’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of breastfeeding and its minimum limit that brings unlawfulness. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is an amount of breastfeeding that makes the flesh or blood grow.’ He (the Imam) then asked, ‘Do you think once can do it?’ I replied, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, I ask you, can twice do it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it cannot do it.’ I kept counting up to ten times breastfeeding.”
